title: An overseer and a dashboard
author: 12OffIntx
selftext:
Is anyone else mental like me and constantly juggling several simultaneous projects and multiple AI subscriptions? I have too many ideas so have 3-4 going at once. One is always my asset desk which is the hub for all my sounds and art assets. Then there are one to two projects I consider "in-flight" and often one in some sort of experimental stage. I utilize a Claude 20x account, a Codex 10x account and a Muse Power account.

Juggling all of this was a chore, especially as I can switch what ideas are active and what are not. I also found projects running into the same issues and making some of the same mistakes. I stupidly took several weeks to figure this out, but I eventually created myself an Overseer and a Dashboard that runs on a local webserver.

The overseer has a few important functions, though it doesn't directly control every aspect.

1. There is a queue system where projects can check out an agent (Opus Medium, Sol High, Sonnet High, etc.) from the pool I have made available. Check-outs are for a fixed period of time and can get extended. The overseer can be given a priority list if I am favoring one project over another in case of contention.
2. It periodically checks the context of itself and each project lead and suggests when a lead should begin the handoff process.
3. Twice a day it polls each active project lead with the following questions:
   1. What went well today?
   2. What went wrong?
   3. What process changes, new tools, or skills would increase either your future development speed or quality?
4. Record the estimate given for each agent turn and the actual time it took to complete the turn.
5. Collect any decisions needed from me from any of the projects.
6. Onboards and offboards projects as I active or pause them.

  
The data from its questions populate the dashboard. It shows me any decisions I need to make with the context behind the question. I can answer from the dashboard and the answer is routed back to the project. Similarly, twice a day I get a list of reflections - the results from the questions asked of each lead. I can Choose to queue, defer or reject each. It also identifies for me if a given process or tooling change would benefit one project or multiple. If a new project is activated it makes sure it inherits shared skills, tools and processes that have been identified as benefiting all leads.

 I am probably forgetting some other things, but I have found the above very useful! If anyone else has done something similar, what things have you added that I haven't thought of  (or maybe forgot to mention)?

comments.author: Austin_Ox23
comments.body: have u considered tracking token usage and costs per projects? could be useful for seeing which projects are consuming the most resources

replies.author: 12OffIntx
replies.body: I didn't mention that, but yes, partially. It is a part of the dashboard for Claude and Codex. It shows percentages left and when the reset it. I even added in a bit where the Overseer is supposed to monitor codex-reset and can flex up the Codex agent pool when an imminent reset is announced. however, it didn't firec correctly the last time so I need to figure out why. For Muse, unfortunately, Meta doesn't provide any good way to pull usage outside of logging into their site in a browser.

comments.author: scarecr0w12
comments.body:
I'd add a recovery drill for those fixed checkout periods: pause an agent, let its checkout expire and reassign the job, then resume the old agent. Can both still modify the same asset or project files? Having each attempt work in its own branch or output folder gives you somewhere to hold the old result while you check which assignment is current.

  
The dashboard could show the project revision each attempt started from, its output, and whether that output has been accepted. For a game project, I'd try the drill with an asset import or a scene edit on a disposable copy. Also try delivering the same completion message twice and restarting the overseer midway through a job. Those tests would tell you whether a restart or delayed message can silently apply work twice.

replies.author: 12OffIntx
replies.body: Some good ideas and things to check, thank you.
